clue.text: Arnold's poem uses the same sort of word for every one

parts.note: to use something is to do it, so this gives the verb do
the word just before, uses, is a verb, so the same sort of word is a verb
every one means each

explanation.surface: A remark that a poem by Arnold repeats one kind of word throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as DO VERB EACH: 'uses' is DO, the same part of speech as 'uses' is a VERB, and 'every one' is EACH, with 'for' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold's best-known lyric, set on the Kent coast, is titled after that shore.

clue.text: Face being ill in bed?

parts.note: being ill in bed is being laid up; in a down light the word laid written upward gives the answer

explanation.surface: A question whether a pale face means someone is sick in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Laid up means ill in bed; in a down clue 'up' reverses, so LAID read upward gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock's face is the dial.

clue.text: See vacant one may be translated to it

indicators.note: translated means changed to another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A bishop's see left vacant, with one cleric moved to Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The Holy See is the Pope's jurisdiction; 'translated' is also the church term for moving a bishop to a new see.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See, the Pope's seat of government, is the Vatican.

clue.text: Restores imprisoned French, on payment, to old district

indicators.note: imprisoned means held inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to renew is to restore
hire is payment for use

explanation.surface: Prisoners of war from France being released for ransom.
explanation.walkthrough: RENFREWSHIRE is a former Scottish county west of Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic Scottish county replaced in the 1975 local-government reorganisation.

clue.text: Malefactor in Eastcheap about to cheat the King

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: split as East and cheap: E for east, and vile in its old sense of cheap or worthless
to do someone is to cheat them
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A villain in Eastcheap, the London street of Falstaff's tavern, plotting against the King.
explanation.walkthrough: Eastcheap is a London street, home of Falstaff's tavern in Shakespeare's Henry IV; split it into E and VILE (cheap), and 'about' puts DO round inside VILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or criminal.

clue.text: Pass cut of meat when sliced

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
to lop is to cut

explanation.surface: Handing round a portion of carved meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A collop is a small slice of meat.

clue.text: Return of service takes love game

indicators.note: a return here is a turning back, so the service's letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services
love is nil in tennis, shown as the letter O

explanation.surface: A tennis rally where a returned serve wins a love game.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennis words mislead: 'service' and 'love' suggest a serve and a nil score, but 'service' means an armed force, and the game is an old gambling card game, not tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is an old card game played for stakes at casinos and saloons.

clue.text: One who is disarmed to meet up with a freak

indicators.note: freak as a verb means to go wild, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone without weapons arranges to meet an oddity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disarmed' reads as stripped of weapons; here it means literally without arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has lost an arm or other limb.

clue.text: Dishonestly travelling as a bishop

definitions.meaning: an old slang phrase for criminal or crooked dealing

explanation.surface: A churchman travels crookedly.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess the bishop moves only along diagonals.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for crookedly, and literally moving diagonally across the board.

clue.text: Artless wingers not replaced by comfortable home team

indicators.note: wingers are the players on the flanks, so take the outside letters of the word
replaced means put back in a different order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a villa is a large comfortable house

explanation.surface: A football team whose clumsy wing players are taken off and substituted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wingers' takes AS, the first and last letters of 'Artless'; 'replaced' turns NOT into TON. ASTON VILLA is a Birmingham football club whose ground is Villa Park.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known English football club playing in the Premier League.

clue.text: Little strip of land has sulphur mine

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A small coastal tongue of land with a sulphur mine on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow point of land jutting into the sea, often sand or shingle.

clue.text: Make a fair amount secretly? That's my affair

definitions.meaning: earning extra money quietly, beyond one's main income
one's lover in an extramarital relationship

explanation.surface: Someone earning a little extra money on the quiet, insisting it is their own business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's my affair' sounds like 'mind your own business'; it names a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a secret extra income and an illicit lover.

clue.text: Superficial evidence of operation

parts.note: read literally, the mark left on the skin's surface after surgery, though the surface suggests shallow proof that something works

explanation.surface: A dismissive phrase about thin proof that some scheme is working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superficial' suggests flimsy, but here it means literally on the surface of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A healed mark on the skin left by a surgical cut.

clue.text: Flower-seller in the theatre sounds idle

indicators.note: sounds signals that the answer is said like another phrase

parts.note: to be idle is to do little

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a stage flower-seller seems lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza is the Cockney flower girl in Shaw's play Pygmalion and the musical My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the flower girl Eliza in Shaw's Pygmalion.

clue.text: Statement of the law

definitions.meaning: the legal calling as a whole

explanation.surface: A legal pronouncement.
explanation.definitionFit: It means an avowal, and the law is a learned calling or vocation.

clue.text: Signal on red — new diversion needed

indicators.note: a diversion sends things a different way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Traffic lights on red and a fresh detour needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signal' looks like a noun about traffic lights; it is the adjective meaning notable.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means striking or notable, much like famous.

clue.text: Unsuitable leader put in question — a charlatan

indicators.note: put in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling question

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A party leader thought unfit is questioned and called a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender who puts on airs, much like a fraud or impostor.

clue.text: Sees calf newly-delivered, quite unrecognisable

indicators.note: delivered anew suggests the letters come out in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A farmer watching a calf being born that cannot yet be told apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking identity or individual features, so impossible to identify.

clue.text: Showing off — knowing about tree

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one word surrounds another

parts.note: fly is slang for knowing or sharp
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone flaunting their knowledge of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaudy and ostentatious, as of a show-off.

clue.text: Scotsman holds extremely evangelical devotion

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: Angus is a typical Scottish man's name

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Scot keeping to a fervent evangelical faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic prayer recited at morning, noon and evening.

clue.text: Speed to stronghold?

definitions.meaning: a secure refuge, such as a fortress

explanation.surface: A question whether speed leads to a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both rapidity and a remote fortified retreat.

clue.text: Delight in cutting heads off

indicators.note: heads off means the opening letters are removed

parts.note: trenchant means sharp or cutting

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm or captivate.

clue.text: Rabbit makes a crisp, golden brown dish

definitions.meaning: British slang: to rabbit is to talk on and on

explanation.surface: A cook turns rabbit into a crisp brown dish.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit on is British slang for chattering.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a battered griddle cake and empty verbose talk.

clue.text: Boy returns to secret sweet-store …

indicators.note: returns means going back, so the name is written backwards

parts.note: Gus is a boy's name
arcane means secret or mysterious

explanation.surface: A lad goes back to his hidden stash of sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant stores sugar in its stem, the source of much of the world's sweetener.

clue.text: … with everything else hard to eat

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and the rest
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Continuing the boy's sweets: with all the rest, they are hard to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid etches metal by eating into it.

clue.text: Drop and damage

definitions.meaning: a drop of liquid from the eye

explanation.surface: Dropping something and damaging it.
explanation.definitionFit: A teardrop falling from the eye, and a rip or rent.

clue.text: Wrongly beginning to suppress complaints

parts.note: ill as an adverb means badly or wrongly

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Grievances wrongly starting to be stifled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailments or troubles, as in a cure for all one's woes.

clue.text: Exhausted, embracing bird? Not very macho!

indicators.note: embracing means holding round, so one word goes around another

parts.note: effete means worn out or exhausted
mina is a variant spelling of myna, an Asian starling

explanation.surface: A worn-out man hugging his girlfriend is told he is not very manly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' invites a British slang reading for a girlfriend; it is the myna bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmanly or womanish, the opposite of macho.

clue.text: Architect using new wood

parts.note: ash is a wood

explanation.surface: A builder working with fresh timber.
explanation.walkthrough: John Nash designed Regent Street and Brighton Pavilion.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash was the Regency designer of Regent's Park terraces.

clue.text: Allowed into unusual Western — the latest is here

indicators.note: into means the first piece goes inside the second
unusual signals the letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: Someone admitted to an offbeat cowboy film, the newest one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' suggests a cowboy film, but it is only anagram fodder; the definition is a cryptic description of a bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin carrying recent news to members.
